title: Why is it colder at the top of a mountain?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why are mountains cold if they are closer to the Sun?
How much colder does it get higher up?
Why is there snow on mountain tops?

explain.say: Climb a high mountain and the air gets colder, even though you are a little closer to the Sun. On average the air cools by about 6.5 degrees Celsius for every kilometre you climb.

draw.text: Why is it colder at the top of a mountain?

explain.say: The Sun heats the ground first, and the ground warms the air touching it. So the air near sea level is the warmest, and air further from that warm ground is cooler.
Higher up there is less air above pressing down, so the air is thinner and lower in pressure. When air rises into lower pressure it expands, and expanding air cools.
Thin air also holds heat poorly and lets it escape to space more easily. That is why snow and ice can stay on high peaks even near the equator, like Kilimanjaro.

faq.q: Why is it cold on mountains if they are closer to the Sun?
faq.a: A few kilometres is nothing compared with the 150 million kilometres to the Sun. What matters is that the air is mainly heated by the ground below, and air gets thinner and cooler with height.
asks: Isn't a mountain top closer to the Sun?

faq.q: How much colder does it get as you go up?
faq.a: On average about 6.5 degrees Celsius for every kilometre of height, so a 3 kilometre peak is about 20 degrees colder than the beach. Scientists call this the lapse rate.
When air expands it pushes the surrounding air out of the way, which uses up some of its own energy. Its molecules slow down a little, and slower molecules mean a lower temperature.
asks: Why does rising air get colder?

faq.q: Why is it hard to breathe high up?
faq.a: The air is thinner, so each breath holds fewer oxygen molecules. At the top of Mount Everest each breath has only about a third of the oxygen it would at sea level.

faq.q: Why does snow stay on mountain tops?
faq.a: Mountain tops are cold enough that snow which falls there does not melt for most or all of the year. That is why even mountains near the equator, like Kilimanjaro, can have snow and ice.

facts: In the lowest layer of the atmosphere, temperature falls by an average of about 6.5 degrees Celsius per kilometre of height.
Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania, only about 340 kilometres south of the equator, still has glaciers on its summit.

quiz.say: A town at sea level is 25 degrees Celsius. Roughly how warm is the air 2 kilometres higher?
quiz.show: 25°C at sea level. About how warm 2 km up?
quiz.why: Air cools about 6.5 degrees per kilometre, so 2 kilometres up is about 13 degrees colder: about 12 degrees.

wrong.1: Air does not stay the same temperature as you climb; it cools with height.
wrong.2: Air gets colder with height, not warmer, even though it is closer to the Sun.
